'''Geoffrey Hoyt Moore''' (February 28, 1914 – March 9, 2000), whom ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' called "the father of leading indicators",<ref name="BLSHistory">{{cite web|title=BLS History Commissioners Moore|url=http://www.bls.gov/bls/history/commissioners/moore.htm|website=BLS|accessdate=23 May 2016}}</ref> spent several decades working on business cycles at the [[National Bureau of Economic Research]],<ref name="NBERHistory">{{cite web|title=Work of Various NBER Figures|url=http://admin.nber.org/nberhistory/nberfigures.html|website=NBER|accessdate=23 May 2016}}</ref> where he helped build on the work of his mentors, [[Wesley Clair Mitchell]] and [[Arthur F. Burns]].<ref>{{Cite journal | doi=10.1177/056943459503900102|title = Following the Indicators| journal=The American Economist| volume=39| pages=15–19|year = 1995|last1 = Moore|first1 = Geoffrey H.|s2cid = 151622165}}</ref><ref name="NYTHershey">{{cite news|last1=Hershey, Jr.|first1=Robert D.|title=Geoffrey H. Moore, 86, Dies; An Analyst of Business Cycles|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2000/03/11/business/geoffrey-h-moore-86-dies-an-analyst-of-business-cycles.html|newspaper=The New York Times|accessdate=23 May 2016|date=2000-03-11}}</ref> Moore also served as commissioner of the [[Bureau of Labor Statistics]] from March 1969 to January 1973.<ref name="BLSHistory" />

In 1946 Moore was teaching statistics at [[New York University]] and one of his students was [[Alan Greenspan]],<ref>{{cite book|last1=Martin|first1=Justin|title=Greenspan: The Man Behind Money|date=2000|publisher=Perseus Publishing|isbn=978-0-7382-0524-3|page=[https://archive.org/details/greenspanmanbehi00mart/page/26 26]|edition=First|url=https://archive.org/details/greenspanmanbehi00mart |url-access=registration|accessdate=23 May 2016}}</ref> later chairman of the Federal Reserve, who would tell ''[[The New York Times]]'' that Moore was "a major force in economic statistics and business-cycle research for more than a half-century."<ref name="NYTHershey" /> In 1956 he was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].<ref>[http://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm View/Search Fellows of the ASA] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616161612/http://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm |date=2016-06-16 }}, accessed 2016-07-23.</ref> In 1996 Moore founded the [[Economic Cycle Research Institute]] in New York City.<ref name="NYTHershey" />
